text:
maria: Heads-up — I ran a 6h canary perf sweep for the recent scheduler/kernel affinity changes. Seeing a ~12% p95 regression on short chat flows (8–20 tokens) after the token-budget bump + kernel routing tweak. Dump attached, brief notes below.
aj: Can you paste the p50/p95/p99 and token-length distribution? Also link to the trace.
maria: p50 +2ms, p95 +14ms, p99 +35ms vs baseline. Token histogram skewed to short flows (peak at 12 tokens). GPU occupancy unchanged. Flame trace shows spikes in the scheduler handoff between prefill queue -> decode queue. KV cache miss rate up ~9% for affected requests. Link: <perf-trace/2204007890>
devon: hmm could be our token-binning thresholds — if small requests are waiting to hit the bigger token-budget they get delayed and then land on a different kernel during decode. Did you check queue wait histograms?
maria: yes — prefill queue wait mean +8ms for the short flows, decode queue wait +5ms. The token_budget target was bumped from 4 -> 6 in the tuning PR to reduce fragmentation, that correlates timewise.
lee: right — and recall we also adjusted kernel selection to prefer wide kernels for >16 tokens. If routing happens after batching we might be forcing small requests into a fallback path during decode (extra copy / memcpy). Could be an ordering/regression.
aj: proposal: 1) rollback token-budget bump for canary, 2) experiment with strict early demux (force prefill->decode routing by token len < 12), 3) enable KV pre-warm at prefill completion for short flows. Run A/B and collect p50/p95/p99 + kv_miss. objections?
devon: +1. I'll run A/B. Also will add tracing tags: kernel_route and kv_miss for each request id so we can correlate.
perf-bot: perf-bot: started job canary-2204-a (rollback-token-budget). ETA ~45m. dashboard: <ci/perf/2204-canary-a>
maria: FYI I also noticed a hot memcpy in the small-kernel fallback path, snippet below: ```c++
if (kernel_choice == K_SMALL_FALLBACK) {
  // falling back to CPU-pinned memcpy -> costly on hot path
  memcpy(dst, src, size);
}
```
lee: avoid memcpy on hot path — consider cudaMemcpyAsync or pinned staging buffer. But first let's see rollback results; if rollback fixes p95 we ship a hotfix and schedule memcpy/GPU-copy improvements in next sprint.
aj: concrete plan: devon runs two variants — A: token_budget=4 + rollback kernel routing; B: strict-demux (<12 tokens) + kv pre-warm. Collect metrics and compare against baseline. If A recovers p95, ship rollback hotfix; if B improves more and doesn't regress p99, consider keeping demux tweak.
maria: created PR #3421 with token-budget rollback + extra tracing. Devon, ping me when helm canary is up. I'll keep monitoring perf-bot.
devon: kicking canaries now, will post numbers in ~1h.
perf-bot: perf-bot: job canary-2204-a completed. Results: p95 improved by 11ms vs current canary (back to baseline). p50 neutral, p99 unchanged. KV-miss returned to baseline. Full report: <ci/perf/2204-canary-a/report>
maria: great — rolling back token-budget on canary and promoting hotfix to prod would be my call. I'll also add follow-up ticket for kernel memcpy -> GPU copy optimization and add KV pre-warm as a separate experiment.
lee: sounds good. I'll queue the memcpy change behind a small microbenchmark to validate no regression in longer flows.
aj: thanks all. devon please link the canary diffs and I'll draft the release note.
devon: linked diffs here: <git/compare/PR3421>. Closing this thread after we confirm prod metrics. :rocket:
